issues.title: stringify() of multiline string with leading space on first line does not round-trip through parse()
issues.body:
### Description

`stringify()` of a multiline string whose **first content line starts with a space** produces a block scalar whose declared indentation indicator does not match the body indentation. The result either silently drops a leading space on every line, or is not parseable by the library's own `parse()`.

At the document root `ctx.indent` is `''`, but the block indentation indicator is emitted as `1`. The body lines, however, are indented with `ctx.indent` (empty at root), so the declared indicator and the actual body indentation disagree.

### Reproduction

```js
import { parse, stringify } from 'yaml'

stringify('  a\n  b')
// => "|1-\n  a\n  b\n"
parse(stringify('  a\n  b'))
// => " a\n b"   ❌ a leading space was lost (expected "  a\n  b")

stringify('  indented\nlines')
// => "|1-\n  indented\nlines\n"
parse(stringify('  indented\nlines'))
// ❌ throws YAMLParseError: Unexpected scalar at node end
```

More cases that currently fail to round-trip:

```js
parse(stringify(' a\nb'))          // throws
parse(stringify('   x\n y\nz'))    // throws
parse(stringify('    deep\nshallow')) // throws
```

### Expected

`parse(stringify(x))` should equal `x` for any string `x`. Each of the cases above should round-trip exactly.

### Environment

- `yaml` `2.9.0` and current `main` (`3.0.0` prerelease)
- Node.js 22
issues.author: Bolt4243

comments.author: AdvaitVarhade

comments.body:
Hi @eemeli, I'd like to fix this issue and wanted to check with you first, per the contributing guidelines on LLM-assisted contributions.

Full disclosure: I investigated this bug and prepared a candidate fix with the help of an AI coding assistant. The change is small and I've verified it locally, but per the repo policy I'm requesting your approval and feedback here before opening a PR.

**Problem** (as reported): `stringify()` of a multiline string whose first content line starts with a space emits a block scalar whose header declares an indentation indicator (e.g. `|1-`) while the body lines aren't indented to match — at the document root `ctx.indent` is `''`. The result either silently drops a leading space on every line or throws on `parse()`.

**Candidate fix** (`src/stringify/stringifyString.ts`, `blockString`): when an indentation indicator is emitted, indent the body lines to match it, threaded through the literal and folded paths — including prefixing the first body line so `foldFlowLines` still recognises content-indented lines as more-indented and never folds them into corruption. Plus regression tests in `tests/doc/stringify.ts`, and one updated expectation in `tests/doc/foldFlowLines.ts` (`More-indented first line (#55)` asserted the old non-round-tripping output).

**Verification**: all 5 repro cases from the issue now round-trip exactly, plus folded-style (`>`), chomping (`-`/``/`+`), nested-mapping, and leading-newline variants. Full test suite passes (1000/1000; the only failures are the pre-existing `json-test-suite`/`yaml-test-suite` missing-data issues, identical on unmodified HEAD).

Would you be open to a PR with this approach? Happy to rework it if you'd prefer it done differently.
comments.author: NYDJustin

issues.title: Empty line after empty tagged value at end of map in sequence is mis-assigned
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
I am dealing with an issue where custom tags with a blank like leads to nonsense yaml being produced.

```
- type: entity
  components:
  - type: InstantAction
    event: !type:CritSuccumbEvent

-------------------------
- type: entity
  components:
  - type: InstantAction
    event:
                                                   <--- these two \n are the issue
      !type:CritSuccumbEvent 
```

**To Reproduce**
I made a little test script to show the behavior, the expectation would be that input and output are the same.
https://gist.github.com/Pachat-Kas/c3816a67a3f21703e882ef9f5862bb07 

**Expected behaviour**
The test script should produce the same intput as the output. 

**Versions:**

- Environment: [node v23.9.0]
- `yaml`: [2.9.0]

**Additional context**
I found some similar looking issues but on closer inspection they weren't related.
issues.author: Pachat-Kas

comments.body:
It looks like the empty line after the empty-but-tagged value is getting parsed as a line before the empty value. Here's a minimal example; the custom-ness of the tag is irrelevant here:

```js
const src = '- x: !!null\n\n- y'
parseDocument(src).toString()
```

```yaml
- x:

    !!null
- y
```

This also happens with anchors:

```js
const src = '- x: &a\n\n- y'
parseDocument(src).toString()
```

```yaml
- x:

    &a
- y
```

And it seems specific to the last key-value pair of a mapping inside a sequence, as this is correct:
```js
const src = '- x: !!null\n\n  y'
parseDocument(src).toString()
```

```yaml
- x: !!null

  y:
```

Calling the resulting YAML "bogus" is a bit miseleading, though, as it's still valid.
comments.author: eemeli

comments.body:
For a lack of a better word I used bogus lol. It wasn't incorrect yaml, just weird. I've been looking into the issue a little, trying a few fixes here and there but nothing that actually solves the issue. I believe it's a problem in the parser, but I could be totally wrong. If I have time I'll investigate further. 
Thank you for your support.

issues.title: No error for C0-control characters
issues.body: **Describe the bug** no error is given for C0-control characters within a string only printable characters are allowed https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#rule-c-printable > To ensure readability, YAML [streams](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#streams) use only the printable subset of the Unicode character set. The allowed character range explicitly excludes the C0 control block[15](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#fn:c0-block) x00-x1F (except for TAB x09, LF x0A and CR x0D which are allowed), DEL x7F, the C1 control block x80-x9F (except for NEL x85 which is allowed), the surrogate block[16](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#fn:surrogates) xD800-xDFFF, xFFFE and xFFFF. **To Reproduce** create a string containing any number of these characters (I can't paste them here in GitHub) ```ts \x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e\x0f\x10\x11\x12\x13\x14\x15\x16\x17\x18\x19\x1a\e\x1c\x1d\x1e\x1f ``` **Expected behaviour** A warning to be provided saying the non-printable c0-control characters are not allowed **Versions:** - Environment: VSCode 1.121.0 - `yaml`: 2.9.0 **Additional context**
issues.author: RedCMD

comments.body:
Yup, confirming this is a valid bug. The lexer is not verifying that the characters excluded from [c-printable](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#rule-c-printable) are actually excluded.

This should probably be an error, though, and not just a warning? And as it's effectively a recoverable error, we should probably only catch it during composition, i.e. in `resolveFlowScalar()` and `resolveBlockScalar()`.
